redteam_note: Comment wording may not match the score — re-read (needs judgement).
revision_notes: Confirmed at 4. The NeGP (2023) confirms INRIS provides digital ID and eKYC and underpins Zamportal service registration (e.g. RTSA, Labour, requiring an ID number); a MOSIP EET authentication layer was piloted from Aug 2024 to connect INRIS to services. Definition: Extent to which the data exchange enables services accessible to all population groups including persons with disabilities, elderly, low literacy
Comments: Zambia internet penetration approximately 48%. Digital services accessible primarily to connected, literate populations. No confirmed accessibility features for disabled/elderly in data exchange documentation. Partial accessibility through Zamportal.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed at 2, though the cited 48% penetration figure is dated and contested. No evidence was found of specific accessibility features (assistive technology, sign-language support, low-literacy design) built into Zamportal or the data exchange. Freedom House (2024) notes online content by and for people with disabilities remains limited, and internet penetration estimates for 2024-25 range from about 33% (DataReportal) to 68% (ZICTA/government figures), leaving a large share of the population offline either way — consistent with 'Partial accessibility'.
